answers.answer: Rule is determined by comparing each player's total warriors plus buildings in a clearing. Tokens and pawns do not count. Ordinary ties mean no one rules; Eyrie wins a tie for most if it has at least one Eyrie piece there. Vagabond cannot rule and cannot prevent another player from ruling.
answers.evidence: Actions → Shared movement, crafting and battle: rule is based on warriors plus buildings; tokens and pawns do not contribute; Eyrie tie exception; Vagabond cannot rule or stop rule.

answers.answer: A normal move takes any positive number of your warriors or pawns from one clearing along a linking path to an adjacent clearing. You must rule the origin, destination, or both, and recheck rule for each move. The same pieces may move repeatedly, including across multiple moves in one action. Rivers are not paths unless an effect explicitly says otherwise.
answers.evidence: Actions → Move (4.2): positive number, adjacent along a linking path, rule at least one endpoint, repeated moves allowed, and rivers are not paths absent an effect.

answers.answer: The defender may play one matching Ambush (birds are wild); the attacker may foil it with a matching Ambush. A foiled Ambush deals no hits; otherwise the defender immediately deals two hits, not limited by defending warriors, and the battle ends immediately if no attacking warriors or pawns remain. Resolve before-roll effects, roll dice (higher result is attacker's hits and lower is defender's; ties give equal results), then after-roll effects. Each side's rolled hits are capped by its own warriors in battle, with Alliance defending reversing the dice and Vagabond using undamaged swords instead of warriors. Add extra hits without a warrior cap, subtract ignored hits, and give the attacker one defenseless hit if defender has no warriors (for Vagabond, no undamaged swords). Each hit removes one opposing piece. The taking side chooses its removal order, but must remove all its warriors before buildings or tokens; it also orders its removal-trigger effects. Both sides deal counted hits even if warriors were removed during the exchange. Whoever removes an enemy building or token scores one VP each, including a defender and outside battle. Vagabond takes hits as item damage.
answers.evidence: Actions → Battle (4.3), six numbered steps, especially Ambush, Roll, Count hits, and Deal hits.

answers.answer: Crafting uses the card's bottom-left crafting icons, not its card suit; each crafting piece activates only once per turn. An item card cannot be crafted unless that item is in the map supply. You cannot craft an identical persistent effect already in your play area.
answers.evidence: Actions → Craft (4.1): crafting icons, once-per-turn activation; immediate item effect requires supply; duplicate persistent effect cannot be crafted.

answers.answer: During your own Daylight, at 10 or more VP, activate a dominance card from your hand into your play area, remove your score marker, and stop scoring VP. At the start of your own Birdsong, mouse/rabbit/fox dominance wins if you rule three clearings of that suit; bird dominance wins if you rule two diagonally opposite corner clearings. Meeting the condition earlier does not win immediately. An activated card cannot be removed or replaced.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions → Dominance (3.3): Daylight and 10 VP threshold, suit win conditions, start-of-Birdsong timing, and cannot remove/replace activated card.

answers.answer: A dominance card that would enter the discard pile is instead placed near the map as available. During your own Daylight, spend a matching card to take an available dominance card into your hand. Available bird dominance remains bird, so it must be taken by spending a bird card; a bird card can pay for a non-bird dominance card. Taking and activating are separate and need no faction action allowance.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions → Dominance (3.3): special discard destination and taking available dominance cards, including bird payment rules.

answers.answer: With two players, remove all four dominance cards, shuffle the shared deck, and deal each player three cards. Place one ruin in each of the four R slots, which occupy building slots. Stock the map item supply with two boots, two bags, one crossbow, one hammer, two swords, two tea, and two coins. Set up factions in letter order: Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond; this is separate from turn order. The summary also describes each faction's standard setup, including starting pieces and placements.
answers.evidence: Setup, Standard Setup steps 1–7: two-player dominance-card removal and three-card hands, ruins and item supply, faction letter order; subsequent faction setup paragraphs.

answers.answer: Only the Marquise may place pieces in the Keep's clearing; other players may move pieces into it. If Marquise warriors are removed from a clearing, Marquise may spend one card matching that clearing to place those warriors in the Keep clearing instead of supply. This can apply outside battle; without a Keep there is no hospital destination. The Keep cannot be placed again if removed, so it cannot be rebuilt.
answers.evidence: Marquise de Cat → Keep: placement restriction, Field Hospitals procedure, and explicit statement that the Keep cannot be placed again if removed.

answers.answer: Marquise Daylight starts by crafting with workshops, then allows up to three actions plus one action per bird card spent outside an action, in any order and number subject to Recruit's limit. March is one action allowing up to two moves; do not interrupt it to spend a bird card or take another action. Recruit places one warrior at each recruiter and can be taken only once per turn; if supply is insufficient, place as many as possible, choosing eligible recruiters. Overwork spends a card matching a sawmill's clearing to place one wood there.
answers.evidence: Marquise de Cat → Daylight and action list: craft first, action allowance, March, Recruit, and Overwork.

answers.answer: To build, choose a clearing you rule with an open slot and a building type, then take the leftmost building of that type. Pay the cost shown atop its column with wood in the target clearing or in other ruled clearings connected to it through an unbroken chain of ruled clearings. Place the building and score the VP shown on the uncovered track space. Building is not legal without the full wood cost, a building available to place, and a legal slot.
answers.evidence: Marquise de Cat → Daylight, Build action: rule, slot, track selection, wood network and payment, placement and VP.

answers.answer: Eyrie Birdsong proceeds: Emergency Orders (draw one card if hand is empty); Add to Decree (add one or two hand cards, at most one bird, to any columns); A New Roost. If there are no roosts on the map, place one roost and three warriors in a clearing with the fewest warriors where all those pieces can be placed.
answers.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties → Birdsong, in order: three steps and the no-roost placement requirement.

answers.answer: After crafting with roosts, resolve every Decree card column by column, in the fixed column order Recruit, Move, Battle, Build. Within each column, choose card order freely; birds are wild. Recruit places one warrior at a roost in a clearing matching the card (two with Charismatic); Move moves at least one warrior from a matching clearing under ordinary movement rules; Battle starts in a matching clearing containing Eyrie warriors and an enemy; Build places a roost in a matching clearing you rule with an open slot and no roost already there. If any required action cannot be completed fully, enter Turmoil immediately rather than skipping it or continuing other columns.
answers.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties → Daylight: Decree order, column order, individual action locations and Build restrictions, and Turmoil trigger.

answers.answer: In Turmoil, lose one VP for every bird Decree card, including both Loyal Viziers; discard every Decree card except the Viziers; flip the current leader face down and choose a face-up replacement, flipping all leaders face up first if none are face up. Retuck the Viziers in the new leader's columns. End Daylight and proceed to Evening. Map warriors and buildings remain. Evening still occurs, including scoring the rightmost empty roost-track space, drawing, and discarding to five.
answers.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties → Turmoil, in order, and Evening, even after turmoil.

answers.answer: Outrage triggers each time another player removes sympathy or moves any warriors into a sympathetic clearing. That player adds one matching hand card, with birds counting as matches, to Supporters; moving a group costs one card per affected move, not per warrior. If the player has no matching card including birds, they show their hand to the Alliance, which draws one card from the deck into Supporters. Supporter capacity still applies; with no bases, excess incoming cards are discarded because the stack's maximum is five. The summary states the no-matching-card draw, but does not specify a separate procedure for a full stack beyond that capacity rule.
answers.evidence: Woodland Alliance → Outrage: triggers, payment, no-card fallback and capacity; Guerrilla War: five-supporter cap without bases and excess cards discarded.

answers.answer: During Birdsong, Alliance may Revolt any number of times first, then Spread Sympathy any number of times. Revolt requires a sympathetic clearing without a base that matches a base still on the Alliance board, two matching supporters, and a legal base slot. It removes all enemy pieces there, places the matching base, places warriors equal to the number of sympathetic clearings matching that base's printed suit, plus one officer, and scores normal VP for removed enemy buildings/tokens. Spread Sympathy chooses an unsympathetic clearing adjacent by path to sympathy, or any clearing if no sympathy exists; it spends the matching supporters shown above the next token, plus one matching supporter for Martial Law when one other player's warriors there number at least three. It places sympathy and scores the uncovered VP. Only one sympathy per clearing; the Keep's placement ban applies. Organize is different: an Evening military operation, requiring an officer, removes one Alliance warrior from an unsympathetic clearing to place sympathy and score uncovered VP, with no supporter, adjacency, or Martial Law cost, but legal placement is still required.
answers.evidence: Woodland Alliance → Birdsong, Revolt and Spread Sympathy; Evening, Organize operation.

answers.answer: Train during Daylight by spending a hand card matching a clearing with an Alliance base to place one warrior from supply in the Officers box; supporters cannot pay for Train. In Evening, take military operations up to the number of officers, in any order: Move once, Battle once, Recruit one warrior at a base, or Organize (remove one Alliance warrior from an unsympathetic clearing to place sympathy and score uncovered VP). Officers stay on the board when used. When a base is removed, discard all supporters matching its clearing, including birds, remove half the officers rounded up, and if no bases remain discard supporters down to five.
answers.evidence: Woodland Alliance → Daylight Train; Evening military operations; Losing a base.

answers.answer: At Birdsong, refresh two exhausted items per tea already face up on the Refresh track, then three more; tea refreshed then adds no refresh during that step. Slip is optional and moves to an adjacent clearing or forest without exhausting boots, even into hostile warriors, and ignores effects that prevent movement out of a clearing. Vagabond's ordinary Move exhausts one boot plus one extra if the destination has warriors of any Hostile faction; it ignores rule, cannot enter a forest, and from a forest may move only to an adjacent clearing. In Evening, if in a forest, Rest returns all damaged items to Satchel and flips them face up, and moves ready tea/coins/bags to tracks if able; it does not refresh undamaged exhausted items. Vagabond always draws one card plus one per face-up coin on its track, even after Rest.
answers.evidence: Vagabond → Birdsong, Refresh and Slip; Daylight Move; Evening Rest and draw.

answers.answer: Explore exhausts a torch in a ruin's clearing, takes one hidden item face up into Satchel or a matching track, and scores one VP if an item is taken; remove the ruin once its last item is taken, freeing the building slot. For a Quest, choose a face-up quest matching the clearing, exhaust its two listed items, and complete it; choose VP equal to matching completed quests including this one, or draw two cards, then draw a replacement quest. Repair exhausts a hammer and moves one damaged item to Satchel without changing its current face; ready tea, coins, and bags move to tracks if there is space.
answers.evidence: Vagabond → Daylight: Explore, Quest, Repair.

answers.answer: Removing one warrior of a faction that is not already Hostile immediately makes it Hostile, except allied warriors removed as battle losses: if more allied warriors are removed than Vagabond items damaged in that battle, the ally becomes Hostile at battle end. During battle on Vagabond's own turn, Infamy scores one extra VP for each hostile piece removed, except the warrior that first made that faction Hostile; ordinary building/token points are additional. There is no Infamy while defending on another player's turn or from Strike. Aid cannot move a Hostile relationship out of Hostile, though it can still obtain a crafted item. Strike exhausts a crossbow to remove one enemy warrior; only if that enemy has no warriors in the clearing may it remove another faction piece instead. Strike is not battle and gives no Infamy.
answers.evidence: Vagabond → Relationships, allied Attack, Hostile and Infamy, Aid; Daylight Strike.

answers.answer: Vagabond cannot activate normal dominance. With four or more players, during its own Daylight at 10 or more VP, it may activate dominance to form a coalition with a player not already in a coalition who has the lowest VP among the other players; it chooses among ties. It puts its score marker on that player's faction board and stops scoring. If the partner wins, Vagabond also wins, including when the partner wins by dominance. Coalition partners are not enemies; a Hostile partner becomes Indifferent. Coalition does not grant Allied relationship powers by itself.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions → Vagabond coalition (9.2.8): eligibility, timing, VP, partner choice, victory, and Hostile relationship effect.
